summary: Henry Thoby Prinsep worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Tonbridge School (~1805–1807) and the East India Company College (1807–1808), and served in the Indian Civil Service (~1809–1843).

Indologist Henry Thomas Colebrooke studied under Citrapati. He served in the East India Company (~1782–1814), held judicial and council posts, taught Sanskrit at Fort William College (1782–1814), and was Director of the Royal Asiatic Society (~1823–1837).

Henry Thomas Francis worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Cambridge (B.A. 1856–1860) under Edward Byles Cowell, later becoming a Fellow at Gonville and Caius College (1861–1873) and Under-Librarian at Cambridge University Library (1877).
Henry Thomas Rogers worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Addiscombe Military Seminary (1848–1849) and later served as Principal of the College of Engineering, Guindy (~1869–1880).
Indologist Henry White Wallis studied at the University of Cambridge under Edward Byles Cowell in 1882. He served as a Fellow at Gonville and Caius College from ~1886 to 1887.

Henry Whitehead studied at Eton College, the University of Oxford, Balliol College, and Princeton University. He held positions at Buckmaster & Moore, Balliol College (1932–1941), the UK Government (1941–1945), and the University of Oxford (1945–1960).
Indologist Henry Whitelock Torrens studied at Christ Church, Oxford (~1823–1828; B.A. 1823–1825). He later served as Secretary of The Asiatic Society from 1840 to 1846.

Henry William Byerley Thomson studied at University College London and Jesus College, Cambridge (B.A. ~1842–1846). He later served as Queen’s Advocate of Ceylon (1858) and Puisne Judge at the University of Colombo (1861–1867).

Henry Yule worked in history, archaeology, Indology, and linguistics. Educated at University College London and Addiscombe Military Seminar, he served on the Council of India (1875–1889) and presided over the Hakluyt Society and Royal Asiatic Society.
Indologist Heramba Chandra Chackravarty studied under Manindra Mohan Bose. He served as a Lecturer at City College, Kolkata, attested in 1977.

Herbert Arthur Popley worked in Indology and religious studies. After studying at Hackney College (~1898–1901), he served as a missionary for the London Missionary Society (1901) and held a post at the YMCA (1921).

Herbert Cushing Tolman worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Indology, and linguistics, earning his Ph.D. at Yale under William Dwight Whitney. He taught at Wisconsin and North Carolina before serving as Dean at Vanderbilt University (1894–1923).

Herbert Fletcher De Cou worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He earned degrees from the University of Michigan and studied at the American School of Classical Studies at Athens, serving as Michigan's Instructor of Greek and Sanskrit (1892–1893).

Herbert Franke worked in Sinology and Iranian/Central Asian studies. After studying under Erich Haenisch and Erich Hauer across several German institutions, he held posts at Cologne and served as Professor at the University of Munich (1952–1979).
Herbert Frederick Samman, a scholar in Indology and linguistics, studied at Emmanuel College (~1890–1892). He later served as Lecturer in Bengali at the University of Cambridge from 1922 to 1935.

Herbert Galton worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at the University of Vienna in 1935 under Nikolai Trubetzkoy and Wilhelm Geiger, and served as Professor of Slavic Linguistics at the University of Kansas (1962–1988).

Herbert Hope Risley worked in Indology and history/archaeology. He studied at Winchester College and New College, Oxford (B.A. ~1869–1872), later serving as Permanent Secretary of the Judicial Department at the India Office in 1910.

Herbert Härtel worked in Indology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies, earning his Dr. phil. at Göttingen under Ernst Waldschmidt. He served as Director of the Museum of Asian Art (1963–1986) and held professorships in Berlin.

Herbert Karl Alfred Plaeschke worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied under Heinz Mode and Karl Ammer at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg, and worked as a scientific employee at the University and State Library of Saxony-Anhalt.

Herbert Leonard Offley Garrett worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. After studying at St John's College (~1899–1902), he taught at Queen's College and served as Vice-Principal (1919) and Principal (1927–1936) at Government College University, Lahore.
